Cc: Paul Metzger <paul.metzger@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redline — clarification on disposition timelines and examples

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking a look at our DPA redline. A couple of points came up in our legal review that we want to clarify before we mark changes:

1) Deletion timelines across storage tiers — your DPA references "delete within X days" but doesn't differentiate ephemeral caches, hot KV, snapshot backups, and long-term archives. Can you provide concrete timelines (e.g., ephemeral cache: immediate on session end; hot KV: 7 days; snapshot: 30/90/365) and which of those you can commit to for onshore processing?

2) Onshore processing example — we need a short, customer-facing example that shows a request from a US hospital user where processing and deletion remain onshore (including transient caches and backups).

3) Proof of deletion — Arcadia needs to understand what evidence you can provide for a deletion request: a certificate, signed audit log entries, or an internal ticketing reference.

Attached is our redline (Arcadia_DPA_redline_v3.pdf). Can you and your legal/ops team respond with suggested language and an example scenario?

We'd like to get this resolved ahead of the procurement review the week of Dec 4.

Thanks,
Samantha Chen
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Arcadia Health Systems

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (Legal) and Laura (Product — infra) to provide the specifics and a short onshore example we can include in the DPA.

High level answers so you have something to work with immediately:
- Ephemeral/session cache: purged immediately at session end (no persistent copy retained).
- Hot KV (used for short-term context caching): default TTL 7 days; we can offer a 0/1/7-day option based on workload & SLA.
- Snapshots/backups: default snapshot retention 30 days for active tenants; archival/long-term backups are 365 days unless you opt out.
- Onshore processing: we can pin processing to a US region and restrict restore operations to onshore personnel and keys.

Karthik — can you propose precise DPA clause language and confirm what form of evidence of deletion we can provide (certificate vs audit entry)?

Laura — any operational caveats (e.g., cross-region replication during failover) to call out in the example?

Happy to schedule a 30-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Dylan — appreciate the quick outline. A couple of follow-ups from our info-sec and procurement:

- For hot KV TTL options, can you confirm whether TTL is tenant-configurable and whether you can enforce a maximum TTL via contract?
- For backups: we need an example of how a restore would be performed in an onshore-only scenario (who initiates, what approvals, how does key access behave). If you can give a step-by-step example that would be very helpful.
- For the proof of deletion: our auditor prefers a signed certificate of erasure plus a correlated audit log entry. Is that something Redwood can provide after a verified deletion request?

We are aiming to close the DPA redline with a small set of agreed language rather than a long appendix. A short onshore example and a proposed sentence for the deletion evidence section would be ideal.

Arcadia Health Systems

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Samantha Chen <samantha.chen@arcadiahealth.com>, Paul Metzger <paul.metzger@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: DPA redline — clarification on disposition timelines and examples

Hi Samantha/Paul — thanks for these concrete asks. Below are proposed DPA-friendly snippets and a concise, customer-facing onshore example you can paste into the contract or an appendix.

1) Proposed retention language (suggested insertion into Section 4 — Data Retention and Deletion):
"Redwood will classify Customer Data into one of the following tiers for the purposes of retention and deletion: (a) Ephemeral session data: purged immediately at session termination; (b) Short‑term operational cache (hot KV): retained for up to 7 days by default and may be configured to 0 or 1 day upon Customer request; (c) Snapshot backup: retained for up to 30 days; (d) Long‑term archive: retained for up to 365 days unless otherwise agreed in writing. Customer may opt out of long‑term archival in writing. For the avoidance of doubt, deletion requests will apply to all tiers, and Redwood will exercise commercially reasonable efforts to purge data from all storage tiers consistent with the timelines above."

2) Tenant-configurable TTL / contractual max
- Yes: Hot KV TTL can be configured per tenant via the Console/API. We can insert a contractual maximum (e.g., 7 days) for Arcadia if required and expose an API flag to enforce it.

3) Onshore processing example (customer-facing blurb):
"Example — Onshore processing and deletion: A US-based hospital clinician uploads a patient summary via Arcadia's application. The request is routed to Redwood's US region (us-west-2). Transient session caches are purged immediately after the clinician's session ends. Short‑term KV entries are retained for up to 7 days (or 0/1 days if Arcadia selects a shorter TTL). If Arcadia requests deletion, Redwood will: (i) mark the tenant data as deleted in the control plane; (ii) initiate background purges of hot KV and ephemeral caches; (iii) schedule snapshot expiration and deletion according to the 30-day snapshot retention window; (iv) if any long‑term archives exist, Redwood will remove the archived copy within the agreed 365‑day window or sooner if Arcadia opts out. All restore operations for onshore‑pinned tenants require multi‑party approval and are executed only from the US control plane with key access restricted to US‑based personnel."

4) Proof of deletion options
- We can provide: (a) a machine‑signed Certificate of Deletion with timestamp and shard identifiers; and (b) an exportable audit log snippet that contains the control plane event ids and user ids that triggered the deletion. The Certificate will reference the Job ID and the snapshot or archive identifiers that were purged.

5) Operational caveats (callouts for DPA)
- Cross‑region failover: in rare disaster recovery events we may temporarily replicate control‑plane metadata to an alternate region for restoration; this is limited to metadata only (no plaintext content) and access is restricted under our DR SOPs. We will include a clause stating that such replication is only used for recovery and will be deleted following the completion of recovery activities.

6) Proposed single-sentence redline for Evidence of Deletion section:
"Upon written request, Redwood will provide Customer with a machine‑signed Certificate of Deletion and correlated audit log entries indicating the control plane job IDs and storage identifiers that were purged, subject to standard investigative timelines not to exceed 30 days."

Attached is a plain text file with the exact markup we recommend for insertion: proposed-dpa-language.txt. Also shared a Drive folder with a trimmed playbook for deletion procedures.

If that all looks good, Dylan — we should propose this language back to Arcadia and offer a short call to walk through the onshore restore/delete flow.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA redline — clarification on disposition timelines and examples (agreed language + next steps)

Samantha/Paul — appreciate the patience while we pulled language together. Summary of agreed points and next steps below. Please consider this our formal response to the redline questions: 

Agreed bullets (for insertion into DPA):
- Tiers & timelines: Ephemeral (immediate), Hot KV (tenant-configurable, contractual max 7 days), Snapshots (30 days default), Archive (365 days unless Customer opts out).
- Onshore processing example: insert Karthik's customer-facing blurb verbatim.
- Proof of deletion: Redwood will furnish a machine-signed Certificate of Deletion plus correlated audit log entries. Redwood will aim to deliver these artifacts within 30 days of a validated deletion request.
- Cross-region DR: limited metadata replication during DR; no plaintext content; replication deleted post-recovery.

Action items:
1) Karthik to drop the proposed-dpa-language.txt contents into a tracked redline and send to Samantha (done).
2) Arcadia to confirm whether you require the contractual max TTL (7 days) or want the Console/API option only.
3) If agreed, we can add a short appendix with the onshore restore flow; I recommend a 30-min call next week to walk through it with your InfoSec.

DocuSign link for a narrow DPA amendment (to lock the TTL/Proof-of-Deletion timeline) is here: https://app.docusign.com/signing/ABCDEFG1234567. If you prefer, we can instead accept the TTL as a product configuration and set a contractual maximum in the Master Services Schedule.

Suggested times to sync: Mon Dec 4 — 10:00am PT or Tue Dec 5 — 11:00am PT. Let me know which works and we'll lock it on the calendar.

Best regards,

Dylan Brooks
